extracted.intended_audience: Contributors and editors submitting or editing OEIS sequence entries
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality criteria for creating and editing OEIS sequence entries: required fields, formatting, notation, program submission conventions, signing, and policies for conjectural data and special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigid entry format / allowed fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries in the OEIS have a rigid format. Each entry contains some or all of the following fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated fields include: A-number, Name, Data, Offset, Comments, References, Links, Formula, Example, Maple, Mathematica, Programs, Cross-references, Keywords, Author, Extensions, Status. Follow the prescribed field structure when submitting or editing an entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-number format
rubrics_metrics.description: The A-number is an A followed by six digits (until we reach A999999).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A005132. Some sequences also have 4-digit M-numbers or N-numbers (from older books); include these where applicable (e.g., M1459, N0577). This is the absolute catalog number of the sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name field conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Name gives a brief description or definition of the sequence; a(n) denotes the n-th term and n is a typical subscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concise mathematical definitions when possible; avoid naming sequences after yourself or acquaintances; use the notation and spelling from the style sheet; the name shall end in a period (or other appropriate punctuation). Sometimes the definition may describe a typical term k rather than a(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data field: content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: This field gives the beginning (at least 4 terms) of the sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally give enough terms to fill about three lines (~260 characters including digits, signs, commas, spaces; DO NOT USE TABS). Terms should be separated by commas. Entries must be integers (base-10 digits). If fractions occur, enter numerators and denominators as separate sequences labeled with keyword 'frac' and cross-reference them. If every second term is zero, normally omit the zeros and list the nonzero subsequence. Label signed sequences with keyword 'sign' and nonnegative with 'nonn'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offset rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The offset is the index of the first term of the sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For lists the offset should generally be 1 (sometimes 0 allowed). For arrays/triangles, offset is index of first row; for regular triangles the first index's offset often equals the second; otherwise give second index's offset in the name. There is a second part (after a comma) that is the 1-based index of the first term >1 in absolute value; server will calculate this for you. Do not repeat offsets or ranges they imply in formulas or comments. For continued fractions use keyword 'cofr' and offset 0 normally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments field conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant information, motivation, and interesting side facts that don't fit other fields belong in Comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are generally chronological (newer at bottom) but Editors-in-Chief may place most important comments first. Except for original author's comments at submission time, all comments must identify the commenter and the date. Use signature formats (e.g., ' - _Name_, Dec 01 2011' or four tildes ~~~~ to auto-insert username and date). For multi-paragraph comments prefer 'From ~~~~: (Start)' ... '(End)'. Corrections may be made in place but should be signed with the correct signature and date.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: inclusion and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: References are for books, papers, and material not found online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include multiple mentions of the same work (e.g., preprint and journal versions) rather than deleting duplicates. Entries should be alphabetized by the last name of the first author; if the work uses a different author ordering, preserve it. When the author is unknown, write 'Author?'; when title unknown, make a reasonable descriptive title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links: inclusion, ordering, and safe linking
rubrics_metrics.description: Links to journal papers, preprints, web pages, illustrations and other material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper is available in multiple locations include all links (within reason). Indicate broken links with '[broken link]' or replace with archived URL. Use stable URLs when available. Place b-file link(s) at the beginning of Links. Index entries go at the end. When a single source has many links they may be combined. Do not use links that trigger execution of compressed/encrypted code; upload such programs as external files to OEIS instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula field: content and notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulas for calculating the n-th term, generating functions, asymptotics, etc., belong here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Spelling and notation section for preferred mathematical notation. In decimal expansions, a formula 'equals' the constant (not about decimal digits a(n)). Give generating functions, recurrences, asymptotics, etc., and cite who submitted each formula where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example field: illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: An example shows how to find or interpret terms when it is not obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give 1–3 simple cases and show your work. For constants give first few digits (to line width). For tables give first few rows or top-left corner. Don't give an example that just repeats the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maple field conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Maple programs belong in the Maple field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please sign and date contributions using Maple's end-of-line comment syntax '# ~~~~' or start with '# Maple program from ~~~~'. Programs should be self-contained except in rare cases. If extremely long consider submitting as a link. Multiple Maple programs should be separated by a line '# Alternative: optional description'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematica (Wolfram Language) field conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematica (Wolfram Language) programs belong in the Mathematica field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign and date using Mathematica comment syntax '(* ~~~~ *)' or '(* Mathematica program from ~~~~ *)'. Programs should be self-contained except in rare cases; if very long, consider linking. Code in the Wolfram Language belongs in the Mathematica section even if executed via Wolfram Alpha. Programs in Wolfram Alpha language are strongly discouraged due to reproducibility concerns. Multiple Mathematica programs should be separated with '(* Alternative: optional description *)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs field conventions (other languages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs in languages other than Maple or Mathematica belong in the Programs field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign and date contributions in a comment. Programs should be self-contained and copy-pastable except in rare cases. If extremely long, upload as a file and reference it (you will see facility when editing Links). Give language name in parentheses at start, e.g., '(PARI)' or '(Perl)'. Keep entries generally chronological but keep programs in the same language together. Preferred comment-signature formats for many languages are listed (e.g., '# ~~~~' for Python, '/* ~~~~ */' for C). Indentation is preserved if a line starts with two spaces or more; it's no longer necessary to replace leading spaces with dots for languages that require indentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-references to related sequences should be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List as a comma-separated list of A-numbers without repetition, with a space after each comma. You may give extra information (e.g., 'Row sums: A000000, A000000'). When there's no special info begin the line 'Cf. '.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords: standardized set
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more standardized keywords must be used to classify sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the fixed set of standardized keywords (see official descriptions and examples). Keywords include things like 'nonn', 'sign', 'core', 'easy', 'nice', 'new', etc.; apply them correctly to indicate properties such as nonnegative, signed, and other attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author field policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Author field shows the author's name and date of initial submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general this field should not be modified from the system-generated value. Sequences with multiple authors can list multiple names. Older sequences may include email addresses; prefer linking the author's name when possible. This field represents the person submitting even if the sequence was known earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions field purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions are to claim credit for additions to the entry that can't be properly acknowledged elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common uses: acknowledge more terms added to an existing entry (e.g., 'a(10)-a(24) from _Name_, Date') or verification of difficult computations. Comments, programs, and formulae are signed and should not be repeated here. Cross-refs, links, and references are usually not acknowledged in Extensions. During approval you do not need to add anything here when editing the sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status field behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Status is a non-editable field showing the sequence's editorial state: approved, editing, reviewed, or proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a sequence is edited the status automatically becomes 'editing'. To show changes are ready for Editorial Board review change 'editing' to 'proposed' by clicking 'These changes are ready for review by an OEIS Editor' at the bottom of the sequence draft. Editors-in-Chief and the Editorial Board manage status changes to 'approved' or 'reviewed'.

rubrics_metrics.name: How many terms to include (guideline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally an entry will give enough terms to fill three lines on the screen, about 260 characters including spaces and commas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 260 characters is a guide, not a strict limit; you may give more but try to stay under 500 characters. If more terms are available create a b-file (common sizes: 10000 terms; can be 1000, 10000, 20000, more in exceptional cases). Editors-in-Chief decide appropriate b-file sizes. If entry already has ~three lines there is usually no point adding more terms to DATA; create a b-file instead. Minimum number of terms required is generally 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing contributions to existing sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: You should sign (add your name & date) when you add something to an existing entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Append ' - ~~~~' to a single-line comment to insert username and date automatically. In programs put the signature in a comment or after a comment-up-to-end-of-line to avoid execution errors. For multi-paragraph additions use 'From ~~~~: (Start)' at the beginning and '(End)' at the end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email policy for contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include your email address in OEIS contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 2011 OEIS does not display email addresses of new contributors. Sign using four tildes (~~~~). To contact authors or editors use the Wiki user page 'Email this user' tool after logging into the OEIS Wiki, or leave a message on the user's Talk page (login required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling and notation preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred spellings and ASCII notations for commonly mistyped words and symbols are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ASCII forms: '>' not 'grth'; '>=' not '≥'; '<=' not '≤'; '!=' or '<>' for not equal; use a/(bc) for fractions rather than ambiguous a/b*c; use |S|, #S, or card(S) for cardinality; use +/- spelled '+-' not '±' and so on. Use 'a(n)' for nth term and {a(n)} for whole sequence. Use binomial(n,k) or C(n,k) (binomial preferred). Follow many specific word preferences (US spellings: behavior not behaviour, color not colour, labeled not labelled, etc.). Use ^ for exponentiation; use Sum_{k=a..b} and Product_{k=a..b} notation; prefer 'prime(n)' or 'p(n)' for n-th prime with guidance on usage. Use 'iff' acceptable. See page for an extensive list of preferred names, symbols, and words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-ASCII characters rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't use non-ASCII characters in mathematical text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ASCII representations of mathematical symbols (e.g., '<=' instead of '≤'). Exceptions: titles of published works, names of authors, places, institutions that require non-ASCII characters (e.g., 'Geneviève Paquin'). Do not use Unicode Greek letters, ellipsis, etc., in mathematical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar preferences and common English mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and common errors in English usage to avoid in OEIS text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: use 'Let k be an integer' (not 'be integer'); 'amount' vs 'number' guidance; 'respectively' vs 'respectfully'; use 'Except for a(5) = 91' not 'Except a(5) = 91'; possessive formation: 'Lucas's theorem' preferred; avoid using a(n) to refer to whole sequence (use {a(n)} or A-number). The page lists many common mistakes and correct forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical definitions clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify frequently ambiguous mathematical terms used in OEIS (e.g., divisors, aliquot divisors, prime divisors, omega/Omega).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which definition you are using when ambiguous. Examples: 'divisors' usually numbers 1 <= d <= n dividing n; 'aliquot divisors' are d < n dividing n; 'proper divisors' officially 1 < d < n but often misused; omega(n) = number of distinct primes dividing n, Omega(n) counts with multiplicity. Always specify if you use a nonstandard definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequences with conjectured terms policy
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle entries where some terms are conjectural or only known by conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally give only terms known for certain in the Data section; conjectured next terms should be mentioned in Comments or Extensions. If many known terms with gaps further along, give known terms up to first gap in a b-file and all terms with gaps/question marks/ranges in an a-file. If only a few terms are certain but a conjectured generating function exists, optionally give both known-values sequence and sequence produced by conjectured generating function. For extremely important problems exceptions are made (e.g., Riesel numbers, Brier numbers) with explanatory comments and hope that inclusion will spur further computation. Mention which terms correspond only to probable primes where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probable primes policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of numbers known only to be probable primes in sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OEIS treats numbers known only as probable primes as effectively primes (on the view they will eventually be shown prime), so sequences involving such numbers are not regarded as conjectural; nevertheless, mention which terms are only probable primes whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for solved famous open problems
rubrics_metrics.description: If you claim to have solved a famous open problem, do not use OEIS to publish the proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First publish your proof in a reputable mathematics journal. OEIS is not the place for publishing major proofs such as Goldbach's conjecture or the 3x+1 problem.
